utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: He was an ethnic Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you speak to this person as to how he received the injuries that we see here?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And can you recall the information that this gentleman gave you?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes. On August 5th, the Macedonian police killed five persons at a home in Skopje during what they claimed was a fierce gun battle with NLA members. We questioned that account. But this person was detained after that operation from the house at which these five people were killed, together with several other people including a 16-year-old boy, and he was beaten at a police station in Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we take a look at the back of this gentleman and the buttocks of this gentleman, were there any particular injuries that drew your attention?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Well, if you look at his back and his buttocks, actually, the white marks you see on the left buttocks came from being hit with a stick. I mean, it's very visible, as well as some of the marks on his back. And that was consistent with the testimony that he gave us.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender this photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P332, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'd like to direct your attention, Mr. Bouckaert, to the events after the 12th of August 2001, after the events in Ljuboten that are at the core of these proceedings. Did there come a time when you decided to go to the village of Ljuboten itself?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And do you recall what date that was?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: It's in my statement. I believe it was August 23rd, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That's the date in your statement. I can confirm that.

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'd like to show you a photograph, Mr. Bouckaert.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If I could ask the Court Officer's assistance, could we look at the photograph that is on page 4 of the court binder. It has ERN number N005-7605. Before I go on, I should have brought this up before. The Prosecution has hard copies of Mr. Bouckaert's statement. If the Chamber would like copies, and the other parties, we can distribute them. That would be of assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Chamber has them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: What we have is the 92 ter statement, if that's what you're speaking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Your Honour. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bouckaert, on the 23rd of August, when you went to the village of Ljuboten, did you drive there?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you have an interpreter with you?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you see this photograph here? It's a panoramic photograph. It shows the area of the village of Ljuboten, looking from the north to the south. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you have any problems getting into the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes. There was a police check-point which consisted of an APC, an Armoured Personnel Carrier, parked by the side of the road on a -- in a field, you know, outside the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Perhaps I could ask the usher's assistance to provide Mr. Bouckaert with the magic pen that is attached to that computer.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bouckaert, just stopping for a minute and looking at the photograph, does the photograph contain the spot where you had to stop at a check-point?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: I can't say it contains the exact spot, but it does show the road where we were stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. But above the photograph, then, can you draw an "X" roughly the area where you stopped at a check-point?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yeah, there. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And what happened at that check-point?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: So the check-point, it was not a formal check-point. The formal check-points had these oil drums filled with concrete or rocks or sand, where you were -- had to kind of weave your way through. This was just an APC parked by the side of the road. We were stopped there. The police officer came up to us, as some of his colleagues stood by the side of the road, and asked us what our purpose was. I was a little bit vague because I did not want to be prevented from entering the village, so I told him we wanted to go look at the humanitarian situation in the village. He then asked us to wait and made a telephone call. He said that he had to check with another officer, and then he came back and said we could go to the village for -- but we had to be out within two or three hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You described this check-point as a police check-point. How did you know that the people there were policemen?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: It was police APC and the people were wearing police uniforms with their police identifications. We passed through those kind of check-points on a very regular basis. There was a permanent check-point just outside Tetovo by the stadium which we had to pass every time we wanted to go in the areas north of Tetovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Just to make this image a bit clearer, above that "X" could you write the letters "CP," please?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honours, I would seek to tender this image now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P333, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Tell me something. Mr. Bouckaert, did you then proceed into the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And did you carry a notebook with you, anything to record information?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What were you carrying with you?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: I was carrying a notebook and a camera.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Can you turn, please, to what is tab number 37 in your binder?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This is 65 ter number 348. It has ERN number N002-5902.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you tell us, first of all, who drew this sketch?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And where did you draw it?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: This is a sketch that I drew in the evening after my Ljuboten visit, because at the time of my visit my -- the sketch in my notebook was distributed over a series of pages. So it's a compilation of those different sketches.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: From your notebook?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right . And why did you draw this or record this information?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: It's just standard practice of our investigations to map out scene of incidents that we're investigating. It is an aide-memoire. It allows us to remember exactly where different locations are, and it also gives a lot more clarity, you know, as part of our documentation practices, basically.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And as you were moving through the village of Ljuboten -- first of all, can we just confirm, does this sketch show roughly where you went in the village of Ljuboten on the 23rd?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: I went to other parts of the village as well, but this shows the area that was affected by the police operation that took place on the 12th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Were you there on that day simply, you and your interpreter, or were you there with someone from Ljuboten village?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: We had gone with a taxi driver who knew Ljuboten village, and then we had looked for some local villagers. I had the name of the -- somebody who was described to me as kind of the village chief, but he was not in the village at the time. So we met another man who introduced himself to me as a school official, who also accompanied us together with a few people, but most of the houses in this area of the village were still empty.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you recall the name of this school official who accompanied you?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: I believe his name was Hisni Murati, but I should check my statement just to check.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Would it help you, then, to refresh your memory?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: With the Chamber's leave, the witness will turn to the paragraph in his statement where this name appears.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Do you know which tab it is? I don't have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This is for the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Hisni Murseli, sorry. That's in paragraph 35.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Paragraph 35.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Let's take a look, please, at the information that's recorded here. First of all, we see on the left-hand side of the -- oh, something happened. We see on the left-hand side of this sketch, we see a road going up to the top of the page. We see a circle with an asterisk inside it, and we see the words "Boskoski house." What information were you recording there?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: There was a house on that street which was pointed out to me as being the house where Minister Boskoski had been present and had been filmed for national television during a part of the operation in Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we move down, we see a street with the name "Ulica 5." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes, Ulica.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And we see a number of rectangles which represent structures. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And we see names inside some of those rectangles. Who do those names indicate?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: They indicate the owners of the houses as they were stated to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Underneath that line of structures, we see a dotted line and the letters "All burned." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And why did you write the words "All burned" there?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Because all of those homes and stores had been burned.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: From that part of Ulica 5, did you then move down to, if I can put it this way, to the right side of the sketch?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes. We first walked down the road, which then kind of goes down, and documented what had happened in that area, and then we came back up and went up Ratak Road, I believe it is, or Racak Road.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We see a Ratak road that goes up towards the right-hand -- upper right-hand corner?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Let's focus, first, on that road that's going down to the bottom of the page. We see a number of squares indicating structures. What kind of information did you record there?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: A number of those homes had also been destroyed or burned. And as you just saw, we also note when these homes were burned or hit. So, for example, the house right on the corner, if the pointer can just go up a little bit, yes, yeah, this house was actually burned from a mortar shell, which set it apart from most of the other houses which had been burned with an inflammable.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if we move up this road that is called Ratak Road, do you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What kind of information were you recording about the structures there?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Again, we were recording whether structures had been burned, whether cars and tractors had been burned. There's a house a little bit further up where 60 lambs had been burned in a shed. We also located -- noted the location of where people had been killed during that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So, if the pointer could stop there and now move just a bit up and to the right, please. Up now, up. No, right there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We see the words "Sulejman Bajrami --"

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: "Killed."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: -- Killed." Who gave you this information about the death of Mr. Bajrami, for example?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: I already had quite a bit of information about the circumstances of his death and where his body had been found. Prior to my visit to Ljuboten, I had spoken to several international journalists and some international monitors about who had visited Ljuboten on the 14th, as well as the one member of the group of 11 people who had been in the basement, who was both still alive and not in custody at the time. Two people were killed from the basement, and the other people remained in detention at the time of my investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very well. Your Honour, I would seek to tender this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P334, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we could keep this document on the screen for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bouckaert, if you focus your attention on the street where we see the street that is named "Ulica 5." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Below that, there's a series of homes or structures. Do you recall entering the compound, if you will, or the yard of a particular home in that area?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yeah, it's actually to the left of those. It's the first house on the left side of the map. No, more to the left. Yes, Kenan Jusufi's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And down below that, it says --

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: "Rami Jusufi killed and car burned."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If you can turn to what is tab 13, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This is 65 ter number 197. It has ERN number N001-4925.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bouckaert, did you take this photograph?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What does it depict?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: It depicts the entrance of the Kenan Jusufi house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And we see a structure -- we see a car or what's left of a car in the foreground, and then in front we see the wall of a structure. Did you notice anything about the walls, the condition of that wall?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Well, the gate had been shot open with some explosive. It's actually the other side of the gate which isn't in the photograph. There were gunshot bullet impacts on the wall which is visible in the picture, and the car had been burned, we assumed and according to eyewitness testimonies we collected, with an accelerant. And it must have been burned at high heat because the rims of the tires actually melted.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We see some bullet damage on the wall in this photograph. Did you find any bullet damage on the inside of this gate or on the inner walls?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: No. We didn't find any bullet damage on the left side of the car, which was facing the entrance of the home, or on the gates or on the wall which would be off to the left side of the picture. This compound is actually visible on the overview map.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That's all right for now. All right. And did you draw any conclusions from the lack of other -- from the lack of bullet damages on the left side or on the inner parts of the gates or on the walls?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: We saw no evidence of outgoing gunfire into the yard of this home emanating from inside the home.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender this photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Actually, Your Honour, that was completely my fault.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It is already an exhibit --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It is already an exhibit. This is P0006. I apologise for the confusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon, the microphone is pointing away from you, and some of your finer utterances are being missed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I appreciate that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If you could turn, Mr. Bouckaert, to what is tab 14 in your binder. Mr. Bouckaert, did you take this photograph on the 23rd of August?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And what does it depict, in general?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Just to physically locate myself, my back would have been to the car that had been burned as I took this picture, so I just turned inside the compound. It depicts the entrance of the house where Rami Jusufi was killed. And in the front of the picture, we found some bullet casings in-situ. There was damage to the front door. You can -- it's a little bit dark, but you can see that window panel on the right side of the door is -- has been shot out at the upper level, but most of the damage was on the other window panel as well as the wood. So it indicated to us that somebody, from this distance of six, seven metres, had shot into the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Just so the record was clear, you said "a distance of six or seven metres"?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you go towards the door and look through the broken window to the interior of the house?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you recall what you saw?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yeah. There was broken glass inside the house, which indicated to us that the gunfire had come from outside and that the force of the bullet hitting the window had propelled the glass inside. And there also was a pool of blood inside, on the carpet inside the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you take a photograph of what you saw on the inside of the house?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And was there a particular reason why you didn't?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: No, it was just an oversight on my part. You know, we had been told that we could only be in the village for a few hours, so we had a lot of work to do within that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek -- excuse me. I won't seek to tender this, Your Honour. It is Exhibit P0005.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If you could turn briefly, Mr. Bouckaert, to what is tab 15 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This is 65 ter number 199.30. It has ERN number N004-4647.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And when we get this photograph up on our screen, I'm wondering if I could ask the Court Usher's assistance to help you, Mr. Bouckaert, make some annotations on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I don't need it enlarged right now, because I can't see it yet. There we go.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bouckaert, this photograph, does it depict the area where you started your observations in the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Can I -- has this photo been taken before or after the Ljuboten events?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: After.

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Obviously, things looked a little bit different, but I recognise the orthodox church. So, yes, this is the area where we began documenting.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. If the Court Usher could assist you, please. If you could take up the magic pen, and if you could draw a circle around what you recognised as the orthodox church.

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if you could place a "1" next to that circle.

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And we've just -- in the prior two photographs where we were looking at photographs from the home of the Jusufi family, can you circle on this photograph roughly where that home was?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yeah. I assume the homes have been rebuilt pretty much in their original positions. So this will be the Jusufi house. [Indicates] And you can see the gate here, and this building is visible in the picture I took. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And to the left of that "X," could you draw a "2," please?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And could you please draw an arrow that would indicate the direction, then, you took along that road to make observations about the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yeah. We first walked up to this house, and then we retraced our steps going in this direction down this road. [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: For the record, the blue arrow is going past the T-junction and towards the bottom left-hand corner of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And the other structures on that street, did you also examine them on the 23rd of August?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender this photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P335, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If you could turn to what is tab 16 in your binder, please, Mr. Bouckaert.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And this is from 65 ter number 197. It's a photograph with the ERN N004-4925-17.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And I believe this particular photograph is described at paragraph 57 of your statement. Mr. Bouckaert, did you take this photograph?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And this house, where was it in relation to the house where you believe Rami Jusufi was killed?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: It should be two houses down. It's actually a shop. It's the burned store which is just at the bottom of the intersection of the two roads.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What did you observe on this structure?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: We saw quite a bit of bullet impact rounds around the window and on the walls of the house, below the window, and those structure had been burned. We saw no evidence of any explosion from shells or RPGs or anything else on the walls. The chimneys were standing. As you can see, the roof tiles had fallen straight down. And the soot on the walls suggested that the buildings had been burned from the inside, which was consistent with the accounts of the villagers that these structures had been set on fire with an accelerant. I should say I'm not an arson expert, but I saw many similar burned structures during my work in Kosovo. So I did feel I could evaluate how this building had been burned.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you find across the street, on the other side of the street from this structure, did you find any bullet damage, anything to indicate outgoing fire?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: No. And we wanted to be very systematic when walking through this area, to check for any outgoing fire, so we did go look through these kind of -- the area that was covered by these windows and walk opposite them to check on trees, on walls, and on other structures to see if there had been any outgoing fire, and we did not find any.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you find -- for example, in this house, did you notice any pieces of shrapnel lodged in any of the walls, anything like that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: No, and also not a spray pattern that you would associate with shells, which I had seen just a few weeks before during my work in the village of Aracinovo, which had come under heavy shelling attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender this photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P336, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If I could turn to what is tab 16 in your binder, Mr. Bouckaert. .

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I am sorry. We're looking for the photo with ERN N001-4925-20.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you see this photograph, Mr. Bouckaert?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you take this photograph?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We see some cinder block walls here in the foreground, and then further on down the street. Were they damaged, from what you could tell?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: The ones on the left side of the street?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: How about on the right side of the street, what does this photograph depict there?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: These -- the actual building with the Ulica 5 sign on it is the same store that we saw in the previous photograph, and it shows all of the buildings, homes, and stores down that stretch. All of them had been burnt, and all of the chimneys are still standing, which to me is an indication that -- again, that there were no explosive impacts or shelling that caused this -- these fires.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: To your knowledge, or in terms of the information that you received on the 23rd, was this damage all caused -- to all of these structures, was it all caused on the 12th of August?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: To structures in this picture, yes, but we did document several homes, including a Macedonian -- ethnic Macedonian home, which had been burned on later dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If you take a look at that cinder block wall on the left side of the road, the fact that there was no damage to that, did you draw any conclusions about that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: It indicated to us that there had been no outgoing fire from this area, and also the -- the police forces who had carried out this attack focused their fire on the right side of the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you recall the information that you received, that there was some structure burned on --

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Sorry. The left side of the road is a part of the Macedonian area of the village, which is one reason why -- probably why it wasn't fired upon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you recall how many homes were damaged on a day after the 12th of August?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: We documented two such homes in this immediate area. They're marked on my map. One is a building on the right, which is just down beyond this last structure visible in the picture. It was burned on the Friday; and then on the opposite side of the road, there was a Macedonian house, a big compound, which had been burned on the Thursday.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And when you're talking about the Thursday and the Friday, you're speaking about the Thursday and the Friday following --

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Immediately after the Sunday, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: -- following Sunday, the 12th?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. And I should point out that the people who accompanied us made it very clear which houses had been burned when. When I went to the Macedonian house to investigate and to take pictures, they said this one was burned afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And by "afterwards," meaning after the 12th of August?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I would seek to tender this photograph, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Bouckaert, the man standing in the right-hand part of the photograph as you look at it, in the foreground --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- do you know who that is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I don't. No. I mean, I can't tell from the face, but -- I'm having difficulty answering the question because he may have been my interpreter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If that's the case, Your Honour, which I didn't realise, if this photograph is admitted, could it be admitted under seal, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The photo will be admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P337, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Could you turn, Mr. Bouckaert, to what is tab 18 in your binder, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This is -- it has ERN number N001-4925-21. It is also from 65 ter number 197.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bouckaert, do you see this photograph?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you take it?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you tell me what is depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: It's the same stretch of homes and stores which had been burned. We're just a little bit farther down the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We see a number of cinder block walls in this photograph. Do you see them?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you happen to look over a wall or the walls to see the other side of them?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes, because of the big windows and the gunfire that we noticed on the walls, which is not very clearly visible, but there was gunfire on the white wall of the building. Yes, we did look over this fence. I remember I stood on this block, actually, to peek over to see if there had been any damage on the high wall or on the low wall which would have indicated possible outgoing gunfire.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And did you see any such damage on the inner sides of the walls?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender this photograph, under seal again, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P338, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bouckaert, if we could turn, please, to what is tab 19 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This is again --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I wonder, Mr. Saxon, whether that might be a convenient time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will have the second break now and resume at 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bouckaert, I'd like to remind both of us that we have to be careful about pausing between question and answers and not allowing our voices to overlap. All right? If you can turn, please, to what is tab 19 in the binder in front of you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This is from 65 ter number 197. It's a photograph with ERN number N001-4925-25.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bouckaert, did you take this photograph on the 23rd of August?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And are we still on the same stretch of road heading downhill from the Jusufi house?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And in this photograph, can you tell us what we see?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes. It's a burned store along the same road.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And we see -- if you look up, we see some roof tiles above the doors and the windows. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you see where the remaining roof tiles from this house were?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yeah. They had fallen straight down, some of them on the street and others inside the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: On the outside -- well, what can you tell us about the damage that you saw to the walls of this house, if any?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: There wasn't any significant damage that I remember to the -- either the outside or to the interior walls to this house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you find any shrapnel marks either in the walls or in the rubble or on the street?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you draw any conclusions as to what had happened to this house?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: As with the other homes, we believed that it had been burned with an accelerant.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender this photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P339, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If you can turn, please, to what is tab 20 in your binder, Mr. Bouckaert.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This is a photograph from the same 65 ter number; ERN number N001-4926-01.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bouckaert, did you take this photograph on the 23rd of August?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And can you recall what information you were given about this home and the owner of the home?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes. This is the home of a Macedonian called Zlatko which had been burned after the events of Sunday, on the Thursday following the events, according to the villagers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did the villagers indicate who had done this burning or who had not done the burning?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes, they did say. As I approached the house and started photographing and looking around, they said this wasn't done by the police. This was not done by the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, again, just to make sure the record is clear, you said, this home belonged to a Macedonian called Zlatko. By that comment, are you referring to an ethnic Macedonian?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: That's correct, an ethnic Macedonian.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. We see, in front of this home, what looks like a gate. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Was that gate locked when you saw it?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And did you see many gates like this in front of homes in your work in Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes. This would be a typical compound of a family with some means, surrounded by a wall and by a gate, whether they are ethnic Macedonian or ethnic Serbs or ethnic Albanians.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I see. And if you just focus on this metal gate for a while, did such metal gates impress you very much?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: I'm --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did they impress you with their security level? Did they impress you as something that would add a lot of security to these homes?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Well, that would depend if I was in an APC or not, but these are not very strong gates. They can be easily pushed over.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And your reference to an APC vehicle, why did you make that reference?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Well, saying if anybody wanted to push open the vehicle -- the courtyard -- the gate with an armoured car, it would be very easy, or even with a normal car.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Had you seen, in your work in Macedonia, homes that had been specially fortified during the armed conflict?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And where was that, for example?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: In many villages above Tetovo which were under the control of the NLA; in the high mountains above Tetovo near the border with Kosovo; and in Aracinovo, the town where very fierce fighting took place in June.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And in these areas that you refer to as under the control of the NLA, what kind of fortifications did you see?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: We found quite a bit of NLA-associated graffiti. They had even marked up their cars with "UCK," which is the acronym for the NLA. We saw sand-bagging; the construction of small brick walls between homes, which allowed fighters to move behind those walls; sand-bagging of windows; some digging of trenches; and, oftentimes, fortified positions at the entrance and exit of villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you observe such fortifications or fortified positions when you were Ljuboten on the 23rd of August?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: No. We didn't see any evidence of any kind of fortification of the village or military NLA activity in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender this photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P340, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If I can just add something to my answer. We focused on the area which was the subject of the Sunday events, so I cannot preclude the possibility -- I didn't visit every house in Ljuboten, obviously, but in the area of this map we certainly didn't see anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Just for the record, I may have given an incorrect ERN number for this Exhibit P340. The correct ERN is N001-4926-01.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bouckaert, could you turn to what is tab 21 in your binder, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This is from 65 ter number 197. It has ERN number N001-4927-05.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bouckaert, did you take this photograph on the 23rd of August?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you tell us what this photograph depicts, please?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: It depicts a shed at the house located next to the house of Zlatko, which is marked on my map, with a burned tractor, a burned trailer, and a burned car inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We see, around the car and trailer and tractor, what appear to be roof tiles. Is that what those are?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Did that indicate anything to you, the presence of all those roof tiles there?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Well, again, there's no other physical damage to the structure to indicate it was hit by a shell. It was a free-standing structure, not attached to any other buildings or structures that had been burned. So this led us to conclude that it had been burned by an accelerant, like the other buildings in Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you find any shrapnel there or shrapnel marks in the walls?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender this photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P341, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If you could turn to what is tab 22 in your binder, Mr. Bouckaert, please.

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It is a photograph from 65 ter number 197. It bears ERN number N001-4927-09.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you take this photograph, Mr. Bouckaert?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What do we see in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Those are the release clips of two hand grenades. I was inspecting a house where one room had been burned, and I was shown these release clips. And the witness told me that two hand grenades had been thrown into his home, so I decided to photograph the release clips for identification purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And those two hand grenade release clips, what are they resting on?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: They're resting on my notebook.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And on the right-hand page of your notebook, what do we see?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: That's one of the pages on which I drew a part of the map; and as I ran out of space, I would go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So it shows a page of your notebook that you used on the 23rd of August?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would seek to tender this photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P342, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm going to skip tab 23.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we could turn, Mr. Bouckaert, to tab 24, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This is a photograph from 65 ter number 197. It has ERN number N001-4927-18.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you take this photograph, Mr. Bouckaert, on the 23rd of August?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And what does this photograph depict?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: It depicts another burned house in Ljuboten, along the same street.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And why did you conclude that this house was burned?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: You can see the roof tiles on the bottom right of the picture. Clearly, the walls are blackened. There was some limited gunfire on the wall. So it was pretty clear that the house had been -- had burned, and we didn't see anything that differentiated this house from any of the other ones which had been burned.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bouckaert, on the bottom right-hand side of the photograph, we see what appears to be a patch of grass. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Down there on that patch of grass, did you find any roof tiles?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did that indicate anything to you?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Again, it indicated that there was no evidence of any explosive impact at this house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Was there any evidence at this house of outgoing gunfire?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: No. I actually -- I did go inside the room through this door and looked at this window, because it did have a good firing position, basically, when people came in. And I didn't see any evidence of bullet rounds or anything else, spent cartridges there, or any fortification or anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: For the record, this photograph is discussed at paragraph 63 of the witness's statement. Your Honour, I would seek to tender this photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P343, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bouckaert, could you turn to what is tab 25 in your binder, please?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It is a photograph from 65 ter number 197. It has ERN number N001-4927-20.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bouckaert, did you take this photograph?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And what does it depict, please?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: It depicts one of the larger homes that we saw in the area. It's the home which is described in my statement. There was a group of, I think, 15 civilians, men, women, and children, hiding in this house when it came under attack. And, actually, it's a three-storey house, so there's a bottom floor underneath the photographed floors.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did this house appear to be fortified in any way?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: No. And I did look -- perhaps on my map you see that this house is right at an intersection, so it will be the kind of strategic location where we would expect fortification because it controls the access to this area of the town. So we spent -- I spent quite a bit of time going through this building, looking to see if there was any sand-bagging or any other fortifications.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So on your map, this is the home that you identified as owned by a Xhefki Huseini [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, could this photograph be marked for identification at this time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, it will be marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P344, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bouckaert, given the location of this house, if this house had been fortified as a strategic point, what would you have expected to see then on or around this house?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Well, we would have probably seen some sand-bagging either on the terrace or around those windows, and the windows would have been open to allow for firing out of the windows. You know, they could have done many other things to fortify the house. They could have built a brick wall where the balcony is right now, a strong brick wall which could withstand some gunfire, but we didn't see any of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you turn, please, to what is tab 26 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This is a photograph that comes from the same series that is described in paragraph 64 and 65 of the witness statement. It has ERN number N001-4927-27.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you take this photograph, Mr. Bouckaert?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What does it depict?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: It depicts the entrance hall to the house that we just saw an exterior photograph of. The entrance to the house would be on the left side of the picture, which is not visible in this picture. There is the propellant part of a Zolja missile, which is a rocket-propelled grenade, in the middle of the room.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can I stop you, please? And just for the record, that is a --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Something just happened. There we are.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: -- that is a greenish-blue object on the floor just above a rumpled red carpet; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yeah. I believe the carpet had -- yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And we see a wall on the upper left-hand side with what appears to be damage to it. Can you describe what that damage was?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yeah. We believe that it was damage from the shrapnel from the warhead of the RPG, of the Zolja.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, if this photograph could be marked for identification, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P345, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If you could turn to what is tab 27 in your binder, Mr. Bouckaert.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It's a photograph with an ERN number N001-4927-29.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you take this photograph?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What does it depict?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: This is a disposable rocket-launcher for an RPG for the Zolja, so it's a one-use type of weapon. You extend it and fire it, and then this is the launcher which is left behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Where did you find this rocket-launcher?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: It was found immediately across the street from the home that we just discussed, the Huseini home.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you find any signs of outgoing fire from that home in the area around the Zolja?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: No. And according to the people I interviewed who had been in the home, there had been a group of, I believe, 15 civilians, including many women and children, inside the home. Those were the only occupants of the home.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And when you say "this group of civilians had been in the home," are you speaking about on the 12th of August?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. There was nobody at the home at the time I visited it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would seek to tender what has been marked for identification as 344 and 345, as well as this photograph that's on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: They will each be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P344 will become Exhibit P344; P345 will become Exhibit P345; and 65 ter 197, page 212, will become Exhibit P346, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm going to skip tab 28.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I would like to ask you, Mr. Bouckaert, to take a look, please, at tab 29 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It is a photograph with ERN number N001-4928-03, again from Rule 65 ter number 197.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You refer to this photograph, I believe, in paragraph 68 of your statement. Did you take this photograph?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, what it depicts?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Just -- it's the compound of Nazim Murtezani.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And what did you observe in this compound?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: The entire compound had been burned, including the structure in the foreground, as well as the home in the back. It was quite a large compound with some agricultural additions to the home.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters kindly ask you to make pauses between questions and answers.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We have been warned.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bouckaert, on the inner sides of the walls that we see in this photograph, did you find any shrapnel damage, for example?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: No. The only damage we found was on the exterior walls, and it was from gunshot fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender this photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P347, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Just remaining with this photograph for a moment, Mr. Bouckaert, it's now Exhibit 347, did you find any signs of outgoing fire from any of these structures?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If you could turn, please --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm going to skip what is tab 30. Actually, I will -- I would like to discuss -- I will skip tab 30. I will skip tab 31.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If you can turn to what is tab 32 in your binder, Mr. Bouckaert.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It's from 65 ter number 197. It has ERN number N001-4928-25.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you see this photograph?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you take this photograph on the 23rd of August?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you tell us whose house we're looking at here?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: It's a serious of houses, but the main house, the burned house, is the house of Qani Bajrami, and it was burnt. And there were three bodies found behind this compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you know if this family ever used another surname?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes, they did. "Jashari" is the other surname.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And for the record, this photograph and this series of photographs are discussed in paragraph 72 to 75 of the witness's statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We see what looks on the left-hand side of the photograph in the foreground, we see what looks like a home with red cinder blocks. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you see any fortifications around that home?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Any big walls?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Any big gate?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: No. There was no gate or walls around this entire compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Any fortification of any kind?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm wondering perhaps, Mr. Bouckaert, perhaps with the assistance of our usher, if you could take up the magic pen again. There is a small green object in the center of the photograph, and do you see that green object?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you draw a circle around it, please?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, what that object is?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: It was another Zolja rocket-launcher.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you find any livestock in this -- at this family home?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: I believe that there were three cows which had been killed in the area of the home.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: But they're not very visible in this picture. They are marked on my map.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. In the back foreground, we see a cinder block structure with a red tile roof. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And then behind that, we see another structure. Can you recall what that other structure was?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes. That's the main house of the Jashari --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Can you see a chimney or chimneys on that house?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Are they standing?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, if this photograph could be marked for identification, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P348, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If you could turn, please, now to what is tab 33 in your binder, Mr. Bouckaert.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It's a photograph with ERN number N001-4928-16.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bouckaert, did you take this photograph?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What does it depict?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: It depicts the Zolja launching tube, again a disposable launching tube that I circled in the previous picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Could this photograph be marked for identification, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P349, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Could you turn, Mr. Bouckaert, to what is tab 34 in your binder, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It's a photograph with ERN number N001-4928-17.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bouckaert, did you take this photograph on the 23rd of August?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What does this photograph depict?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: It's another photograph of the same Jashari house that was seen in the picture two previous.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We see in the bottom foreground, we see what appears to be a large yellow tank. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What was that tank used for, if you know?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: I believe it's used for irrigation of fields. It's a water tank.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And what did you observe about the remnants of this house?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: We did spend quite a bit of time looking around this house, because three people had been killed while fleeing from this house, so we looked in the windows. There was a lot of rubble inside the house, so it was difficult to tell, because the roof and the building had collapsed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Had collapsed?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Had fallen down. So -- but we didn't see any evidence that there had been any shooting from inside the house. We also looked at all of the trees and walls and other structures opposite the house -- opposite the windows to see if there had been any shooting, and we didn't find anything of that nature.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bouckaert, on the outside walls of this house, sort of up above the ground, we see some marks. Do you recall what those marks were?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yeah. I believe that they were gunfire, and we found similar gunfire directed at the upper part of the building at the front of the house. I believe it's visible in the picture that we saw previously.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: In the center of the photograph, sticking up above what used to be the roof of the house, we see a dark-coloured structure. What is that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: That's the chimney of the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender this photograph, as well as the photographs that have been marked for identification, as Exhibits P348 and 349.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The three will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This photograph will become Exhibit P350; whereas, P348 will become Exhibit P348, and P349 will become Exhibit P349.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bouckaert, if we can remain on this photograph, I believe you said you looked in through the windows. On the sides of the inner walls, did you find any damage, any shrapnel marks?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I believe you mentioned earlier in your testimony, Mr. Bouckaert, that before and after your visit to Ljuboten, you met with some of the witnesses of the events of the 12th of August. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you turn, please, to what is tab 12 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It's a photograph from 65 ter 197. It bears ERN number N001-4925-03.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bouckaert, did you take this photograph?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Whom does it depict?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: It depicts a resident of Ljuboten who I interviewed in Skopje. I believe his name is Ejup Hamiti.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: For the record, this photograph is discussed at paragraph 51 of the witness statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you recall what Mr. Hamiti told you about his experience on the 12th of August?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes. He first told me about the shelling that took place on Friday and Saturday in which several people that he knew had been killed, and then he told me about his flight from the village together with a large group of people from Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: He appears to have an injury to what looks to be the left side of his head. Did he tell you how he got that injury?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes. It was a superficial gunshot wound from policemen at a check-point.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Subsequently, did you write a report about your investigation into the events in Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And did you contain the information provided by Mr. Hamiti in your report?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes. Just on this one incident at the police check-point, we interviewed three separate people: Him, another young man who had also been beaten unconscious, and the mother of this young man.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This young man, Mr. Hamiti?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender this photograph now, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P351, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You mentioned a short time ago that you had written a report about the investigation that you did in the events in Ljuboten. Why did you do that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Because that's our standard practice. As Human Rights Watch, we investigate abuses, war crimes, crimes against humanity, and we write public reports about it after we complete our investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you turn to what is tab 36 in your binder, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This is from 65 ter number 235, and fortunately or unfortunately -- well, no, it does appear to have only one ERN. It begins with ERN U0000098. We see a letter there. Can we go to the next page, please, in both languages. This document, it says the word "Macedonia" up in the top right-hand corner. We see the words "Human Rights Watch" on the upper left-hand corner. On the upper right side, we see"September 2001"; and below, there's a photograph there. Below the photograph, we see a title. It says: "Crimes Against Civilians, Abuses by Macedonian Forces in Ljuboten, August 10-12, 2001."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you see that, Mr. Bouckaert?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Who wrote this report?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, for example, the information that was included in this report, where did it come from?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: It came from my interviews with eyewitnesses, victims, journalists, observers, political figures, and other sources that I interviewed relating to the events in Ljuboten, as well as public statements by Macedonian officials.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you also include information or things that you had observed on your visit to the village of Ljuboten on the 23rd of August in this report?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes. This report combines the testimonies that we collected with the physical evidence and compares the two in terms of credibility, assessing credibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Just a point of clarification now. Did you interview or try to interview then Minister Boskoski or other high-level members of the Ministry of the Interior before you wrote this report?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you tell us why?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Because we had security concerns. I discussed with my executive director, and we thought that it would not be wise to seek a formal interview with the Minister or senior police officials at the time. It might endanger my security as well as the security of the information that we had collected.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you know if the Minister had already made the public statements about the events in Ljuboten before you wrote your report?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes. On August 14th, there were some OSCE observers and journalists who gained access to Ljuboten while the bodies were still present, and they carried -- they saw the bodies. One of the OSCE observers made some probably unauthorised comments to the media, and Mr. Boskoski reacted very angrily to those unauthorised statements, accusing the OSCE of interfering with the mandate of the police, of usurping the right to investigate crimes, and that statement is actually quoted in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you recall to whom was your report sent after its publication? To whom did Human Rights Watch send this report?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Our report and the accompanying press release is literally sent to thousands of people. They include journalists, diplomats, Macedonian officials, as well as the public at large, and they are made public on our website.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bouckaert, I'm sorry, it's my fault. My question was much too broad. Do you know whether this report was sent to particular officials of the Macedonian government at that time?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And can you tell us which Macedonian government officials this report was sent to?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: According to our records, it was sent to the Prime Minister's office; to the Foreign Minister; and to the Embassy in Washington, D.C., the Macedonian Embassy in Washington, D.C., at the very least. We don't have any record of it being sent to the Minister of Interior directly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Is it possible that it was sent to the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes, it certainly is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That's not a very useful question or answer, you'll understand, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we could turn, please, to the third page of the report, and also the third page in the Macedonian version, please. If we could turn to the next page, please, in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We see here the word "Summary." And at the start of the third paragraph, we see the sentence: "Macedonian police forces committed serious abuses during their three-day operation in Ljuboten." Do you see that, Mr. Bouckaert?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The following paragraph begins: "During their Sunday attack, police fired indiscriminately into the homes of civilians." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: A couple sentences later, we see: "The Macedonian police also burned at least 22 houses, sheds, and stores along their route using gasoline to set many of them aflame." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes. I just want to point out, in our summary, we don't footnote this information, but it's obviously documented in much greater detail in the report itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The next paragraph begins with: "The abuse continued for the hundreds of ethnic Albanian citizens who tried to flee Ljuboten." A couple of sentences below: "Over 100 men were arrested and taken to police stations in Skopje, where they were subjected to severe beatings." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The next paragraph begins with the sentence: "The Ljuboten operation was carried out by the Macedonian Ministry of Interior's regular and reservist police troops."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And then for those following along in Macedonian, on the next page of the Macedonian version, the same page in the English version, we see a sentence: "The abuses committed by the Macedonian police are among the most serious committed so far in Macedonia's 6-month-old conflict."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you see that, Mr. Bouckaert?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: On the next page in the English version, if we could stay on the same page in Macedonian, we see the word "Recommendations" in the middle, followed by the words in bold "To the Macedonian government," and below it says: "Investigate and prosecute the persons responsible for the abuses in Ljuboten. Conduct a credible and partial and transparent investigation into the allegations of government abuses in Ljuboten, including the role of Minister of the Interior Ljube Boskoski and the forces under his command."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes. And -- yeah, and there's one more sentence in terms of what kind of investigation we were requesting, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: In other words, the following sentences talk about an independent investigation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: "Independent from the government agencies involved in the Ljuboten operation, particularly the Minister of the Interior."

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we could turn now, please, to what is the bottom of page 7 in the English version and the top of page 9 in the Macedonian version. I'm sorry. If we could see the bottom of page 7 in the English version, please. It says "7" at the bottom of the page. So it's two pages further along.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: At the bottom of that page, there's a paragraph talking about a Human Rights Watch visit to the home of Elmaz Jusufi. Do you see that, Mr. Bouckaert?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And then it talks about a physical scene consistent with his account. The gate to the yard had been blown away by an explosion. There was a burned-out hulk of a car. Bullet casings were found lying in the yard about six metres from the front door. Apparently, the shots fired at Rami Jusufi.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we turn now to what is the next page in the English version and page 10 of the Macedonian version, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
