utterances.text: The bottom of the page in the English version, we see a paragraph begins with: "During an August 23 visit to Ljuboten." Do you see that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It continues: "Human Rights Watch researchers inspected, photographed, and documented all of the burned homes in the village, and our findings were consistent with the accounts of the villagers. Human Rights Watch counted a total of 22 homes, stores, and sheds that had been set on fire or caught fire from shelling on August 12th. In addition, the house of a Macedonian resident had been burned on August 16, 2001, possibly in revenge by ethnic Albanians, and at least one other Albanian home was then burned by Macedonian police during August 17, 2001."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we turn to the next page in the English version, please, and we'll continue at the bottom of page 10, the page we're on in the Macedonian version.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: On this page in English, we see a discussion of information provided by Mr. Aziz Bajrami, and we see a sentence -- or a paragraph beginning: "Aziz Bajrami and his sons were then ordered to lay down next to the men." Do you see that, Mr. Bouckaert?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It then continues: "Soon thereafter, one of the police officers kicked 21-year-old Sulejman in the head, and the boy stood up stunned, tried to run away, and was shot down. The police officers then ordered Aziz Bajrami and another elderly man, 68-year-old Muharrem Bajrami, to leave the scene. Aziz Bajrami quickly ran away, but heard gunshots behind him, as Muharrem was shot dead." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we could turn now, please, to page 12 of the English version and the end of page 13 and the beginning of page 14 in the Macedonian version. I'm sorry. Could we go two pages further on in the English version?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We see there a paragraph beginning with: "The most severe violence." Do you see that? The second full paragraph, do you see that, Mr. Bouckaert?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes. And "the most severe" in this context is talking about the most severe violence faced by civilians who fled, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Right. The second sentence in this paragraph, it says: "A number of fleeing villagers from Ljuboten were brutally beaten by masked ethnic Macedonian civilians close to the Radisani police check-point in the presence of Macedonian police officers." Then there's a description of information given by the young man who we saw earlier, Ejup Hamiti, who had the wound to his head. And then if we go further down on that same page in the English and to the top of the next page in the Macedonian version, we see how a woman named Safi Fetahu relates how a police officer told her husband, "Where were you, you terrorist?" And the policeman said again, "Oh, no, more friends, only death is waiting for you." "He said to my 20-year-old son Dilever also, 'You were in the NLA and now you want to go to Skopje. Now you will see what awaits you.'" Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This information that we've gone over, is this information that you collected during your investigation?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes. And it's all sourced and footnoted to let the reader know where we got the information from. The footnotes say the date and the place and, in most cases, the names of the people we interviewed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we turn now to what is at the bottom of -- what is marked page 14 in the English version. It has ERN number U0000111 at the top, and it would be page 15 of the Macedonian version. It would be two pages further along from the page that's on the screen right now in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: On this page, in the middle of the page in English, Mr. Bouckaert, there's a paragraph beginning: "The Prolica police station was full." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And you're quoting one of the persons you interviewed, and it goes on to say: "Full with police officers and also some civilians. Most of the police were masked." And then: "They took us out of the vans and beat us on the way into the police station." The next paragraph: "They started beating us again very brutally. Police officers would just come in and beat us, for four or five hours they beat us." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we could turn to the next page in the English version and page 16 of the Macedonian version, and, Your Honour, I'm almost finished with this document. If we could go forward one page in the English version, please. It has ERN number U00001112. That's fine. That's correct. We see a subheading -- no, we've lost it now. This too shall pass.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We see a subheading: "The Responsibility of the Security Forces and the Role of the Minister of the Interior Boskoski." Do you see that, Mr. Bouckaert?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That begins with: "The Macedonian security forces that carried out the abuses documented in this report belong to the Minister of the Interior, which is responsible for all police forces in Macedonia." Why did you make this statement in your report?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT
utterances.text: Because that was a conclusion of our research.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this point I would seek to mark this document for identification, pursuant to your order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P352, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, I am aware of the time. Perhaps this is the moment to stop.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Saxon. We do need to stop now. We will resume tomorrow at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 3rd day of July, 2007, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.02 p.m.,
